title: Union City 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Union City 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Union City 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Union City industrial along I-880, Union Landing retail, and BART transit-village multifamily near the intermodal station.

sections.html: Union City built one of the Bay Area's earliest transit-oriented development projects around its BART intermodal station, and that early bet on density still shapes what an exchanger finds here today. Industrial and distribution buildings line the I-880 corridor toward Fremont and Hayward, Union Landing anchors the retail side of the market, and multifamily near the station commands a premium tied directly to the intermodal connection. An exchanger working this market usually chooses among those three categories rather than finding much crossover between them. Union City's position between Fremont and Hayward also means it draws comparison shoppers and industrial tenants from both directions, which keeps demand steadier here than in a city that sits at the edge of a single labor market rather than between two of them.

sections.heading: Union Landing and Big-Box Retail Along I-880
sections.html: Union Landing draws shoppers from across the southern Alameda County, and the power-center format there leans on big-box anchors with smaller in-line tenants filling the remaining space. Lease terms on anchor space run long, often ten years or more with renewal options, while in-line tenant turnover happens more frequently, and a buyer identifying a Union Landing parcel should confirm which category the specific building falls into before assuming a stabilized rent roll for the full term. Co-tenancy clauses tied to a major anchor's continued occupancy are common in this kind of power center, and a buyer should review those clauses carefully, since losing an anchor tenant can trigger rent reductions or early termination rights for smaller in-line tenants.

sections.heading: Industrial and Distribution Space Between Fremont and Hayward
sections.html: Union City's industrial stock sits in the corridor connecting Fremont's manufacturing base to Hayward's older warehouse inventory, and buildings here serve a mix of regional distribution and light assembly tenants. Clear height and truck court depth vary meaningfully across this corridor, and a replacement property buyer should confirm the specific building's specifications match what the current or a prospective tenant actually needs rather than relying on square footage alone, since an older Union City warehouse built decades ago may not meet modern clear-height standards.

sections.heading: The Station District and Transit-Oriented Multifamily
sections.html:
Multifamily developed around the Union City BART station reflects one of the region's oldest transit-village concepts, dating back to a planning effort that predates most of the transit-oriented development now common across the Bay Area, and buildings closest to the platform generally command higher rents than comparable product a half-mile away. A diligence file for Union City station-area multifamily typically includes:

  • Trailing rent roll with proximity-based rent comparison across the property
  • Parking ratio confirmation against station-area zoning
  • BART ridership and service-frequency documentation supporting rent premium claims
  • Seismic retrofit records for any pre-1990s buildings
  • Capital expenditure and deferred maintenance history
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

A buyer should walk the distance from the building to the actual station entrance rather than relying on a map radius, since grade changes and street crossings can add real walking time that affects the rent premium the property can actually support.

sections.heading: Identification Strategy When BART Proximity Drives Value
sections.html: Because station proximity affects value so directly in Union City, exchangers often use the three-property rule to name a small set of specific station-adjacent buildings rather than casting a wide net, since properties a mile or more from the platform behave more like ordinary suburban product and do not carry the same premium. Naming both a closer, higher-priced candidate and a farther, more affordable one gives the exchanger a fallback if financing on the premium property does not clear underwriting in time.

sections.heading: Boot Exposure When Trading Up From Smaller East Bay Holdings
sections.html: An exchanger moving from a smaller Hayward or San Leandro property into a larger Union City building should confirm the relinquished-property proceeds and any assumed debt are structured to avoid unintended boot, since receiving cash back or reducing debt load without replacing it can trigger a partial taxable gain. The qualified intermediary should model this before the exchange agreement is signed; this description covers process only, and a tax advisor should confirm the final boot calculation.

faqs.q: Is Union Landing anchor space or in-line space the better replacement property?
faqs.a: It depends on the lease structure. Anchor space typically carries longer terms with renewal options, while in-line tenants turn over more often, so confirming which category applies to the specific parcel matters before underwriting a stabilized rent roll.

faqs.q: What should I check on an older Union City warehouse?
faqs.a: Confirm clear height and truck court depth against what current or prospective tenants actually require, since older buildings in this corridor were often built to standards below what modern distribution tenants expect.

faqs.q: Does distance from the BART station really affect Union City multifamily rents?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is worth walking the actual route rather than measuring a straight-line radius, since grade changes and street crossings can add real walking time that reduces the rent premium a property farther from the platform can support.

faqs.q: Why identify both a close and a farther Union City property?
faqs.a: Naming a premium station-adjacent building alongside a more affordable fallback under the three-property rule gives the exchanger a path forward if financing on the higher-priced candidate does not clear underwriting before the 45-day deadline.

faqs.q: What is boot, and why does it matter when trading up into Union City?
faqs.a: Boot is cash or debt relief received in an exchange that was not offset by new debt or added cash, and it can trigger a partial taxable gain, so an exchanger moving into a larger Union City property should have the intermediary model this before signing.
